claims.text: First: pulse oximetry, ECG and chest x-ray in most patients.
claims.quote: Most patients should initially have pulse oximetry, ECG, and chest radiographs.

claims.text: Serial troponin and ECGs when symptoms suggest acute coronary syndrome, since one normal set does not rule out a cardiac cause.
claims.quote: Because a single normal set of cardiac biomarkers does not rule out a cardiac cause, patients whose symptoms suggest an acute coronary syndrome should have serial measurement of the cardiac biomarker troponin and serial ECGs.

claims.text: Cath within 90 minutes for ST elevation or high-risk NSTEMI.
claims.quote: Immediate catheterization is indicated in patients with ST-elevation on ECG or in patients with non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) plus high-risk features (eg, hypotension, ventricular arrhythmias, persistent chest pain despite optimal medical management), or high risk score (GRACE risk score [3]). In these patients, catheterization within 90 minutes of arrival is considered standard of care.

claims.text: POCUS or echocardiography in unstable patients, to look for ventricular dysfunction, valve disease, effusion or tamponade.
claims.quote: Sometimes, particularly in patients with hemodynamic instability, either a point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) or a complete echocardiogram can also be useful in further evaluating potential life-threatening causes (2). Echocardiography can be particularly useful in identifying left ventricular or right ventricular dysfunction, evidence of right ventricular pressure overload, valvular pathology, pericardial effusions, and signs of pericardial tamponade.

claims.text: Abnormal aortic contour on chest x-ray calls for testing for thoracic aortic dissection.
claims.quote: abnormal aortic contour on chest radiograph suggests need for testing for thoracic aortic dissection

claims.text: D-dimer for possible pulmonary embolism in low- or intermediate-risk patients.
claims.quote: If a pulmonary embolism (PE) is considered possible, D-dimer testing is done in patients who are at low or intermediate risk.
